output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by a new vendor edge rule, not by release 6.14. A Corvane rule pack went live on 3 March at 10:38 UTC. It added rule AUTO-LIB-17, which blocks (HTTP 403) password requests whose user-agent is the networking library nettle-http and that carry no edge session cookie. Our Android app uses that library for every call. The failures began at 10:41 on every app version within a minute, which shows the 6.14 rollout is not the cause. That rollout was only 5% of attempts, and the older versions fail at the same rate. Quick-unlock and iOS are unaffected. The blocked traffic comes from about 41,300 installs, and 92% of them had a successful login in the previous 90 days, so these are real customers, not bots. OS patch level makes no difference. Do not roll back 6.14. Do not raise bot sensitivity. Do not exclude blocked attempts from the KPI, because that would hide the problem. Next, ask Corvane to set the AUTO-LIB-17 rule to log-only on the mobile password path. Keep rate limits, lockout and the other rules active. Then confirm in telemetry that password success returns to about 96%. Let the 6.14 rollout continue while you track outcomes by app version. I'm quite confident. The link to the extra call volume is unproven, because the fee mailing is a competing explanation.
